messages:
sam: FYI I opened Terraform PR #5123 to introduce a per-model ConfigMap (name=\"model-configs\") for runtime knobs / feature flags. Want to discuss rollout strategy — we don't want to bounce all model-server pods. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/5123

lina: looked at the plan briefly — TF will create the ConfigMap with keys like enable_llm_cache, kv_cache_size, model_overrides. Default values are conservative.

infra-bot: terraform plan shows: + kubernetes_config_map.model-configs (will be created) — no other resources changed in this plan.

ashley: quick notes: mounting a ConfigMap as a volume lets the POD see file updates without restart, but many app processes only read flags at startup. So updating the CM alone may not flip behaviour until restart.

mike: TF k8s provider often 'replaces' resources when certain fields change, but ConfigMaps are mutable. The real problem is how the app picks up changes — either watch files or we trigger a rolling restart.

ashley: I recommend using a checksum annotation on the Deployment pod template to control restarts per-deployment, e.g. metadata.annotations: \"cm.redwood.com/model-configs-checksum\". That way we can patch a single deployment to roll it. Example: 

```
kubectl patch deploy model-server-bert -n models 
  -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"cm.redwood.com/model-configs-checksum":"b3f1c9a"}}}}}'
```

mike: alternative is to let TF manage that annotation so deployments get updated as part of the apply, but that requires Terraform to compute the CM hash (templatefile + sha256). If we want manual canary, do the patch route.

lina: also callout: per-model secrets are separate (model-auth-keys). Make sure the secret-sync job runs before we enable any new per-model flags that rely on secrets. I saw one env var in the PR referencing secretRef: model-api-key.

sam: proposed rollout plan:
1) apply ConfigMap to staging namespace (TF apply or kubectl apply to staging)
2) run a single canary: patch model-server-bert with the checksum annotation above and watch traces/latency for 10–15m
3) if canary looks good, patch other critical models one-by-one by label (model=critical)
4) if everything green, promote to prod via TF apply (or drive the same annotation updates in prod)

ashley: I can run the staging canary at 16:00 PT. Checklist for canary:
- create backup of current configmap: `kubectl get cm model-configs -n models -o yaml > cm.backup.yaml`
- compute checksum of the new CM data: `sha256sum new-model-configs.yaml | awk '{print $1}'`
- patch deployment with the checksum (command above)
- watch logs and dashboards (latency, error-rate, token-serving time)

infra-bot: CI note — dry-run plan/validate job queued for PR #5123: https://ci.internal/runs/2345 (plan succeeded). :eyes:

mike: small terraform tip: if TF will be the source of truth for the ConfigMap in prod, add a `lifecycle { ignore_changes = ["metadata.annotations"] }` to the deployment resource so transient annotation updates don't get reverted, or instead set the annotation in TF from a computed sha256(file) value.

lina: also make sure monitor alerts are muted for the canary window or we'll get paged. I'll open a quick alert-snooze linked to the canary deployment label.

sam: perfect. @ashley can you take ownership of the canary? ping here when you start and when you finish. If you hit anything weird, revert using the backup you made. :thumbsup:

ashley: taking it. will run at 16:00 PT and report back here. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled patch to model-server-bert in staging at 16:00 PT (dry-run).

mike: one more gotcha — if the app reads kv_cache_size at startup only, we'll need a graceful restart window so KV caches rebuild without thundering herd. Consider staggering restarts by pod with `kubectl rollout restart --grace-period=30 --timeout=5m` per-pod.

sam: noted. we'll stagger by pod for critical models. thanks everyone.

lina: thanks — I'll add these steps to the PR description and include the checksum example and canary checklist.

ashley: canary done at 16:14 PT — no regressions observed, latency stable, no errors in auth. Rolling to next 3 critical models now. Will update when all done. :rocket:
